pairs.subject: module-design
pairs.evidence: src/athena/proving/roles.py:480 Every role call passes through RoleCaller, which hides the purse check, the run-log row and the schema validation behind call/call_json, and the clients behind it are swappable at the HttpPost and Runner fields, so the Proving Ground core is deep and has real seams.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/proving/roles.py:480 Two methods hide the budget, the ledger row, validity counting and JSON shape checks; a bad answer is a counted result, not a caller concern.

tests/proving/conftest.py:3 Fakes plug in at HttpPost, Runner and build_local's model_fn, so the gate, catalog and brain under test are the production classes; an offline lane refuses any network call a test did not fake.
src/athena/proving/budget.py:99 Budget is pure accounting with no I/O (cost in, state out), so its tests need no doubles.
src/athena/proving/roles.py:166 The async engine stream is collected in one call at the edge; the rest of NebiusRole and RoleCaller is synchronous. The offloaded region is a single call.

src/athena/proving/roles.py:182 One pass builds several outputs (text, token counts, cost, served model, finish reason) and returns early on an error. That is explicit sequential code, which the rule's condition 1 calls for.
src/athena/proving/budget.py:11 The accumulators that cross worker lanes (Budget, Validity, RunLog) are shared by reference behind locks, not copied per lane, so no lane's totals are lost.

src/athena/proving/world.py:372 The method-assign hatch is marked with its error code, enclosed in World._observe, one line per wrapped method, and the docstring states the invariant ('Observation only').
src/athena/proving/report.py:27 The text-encoding decision has one home, and roles.py and runlog.py import it instead of re-encoding the choice themselves.

pairs.subject: module-design
pairs.evidence: src/athena/core/brain/store.py:304 The brain disables SQLite's thread-affinity check and replaces it with the write lock, but the public writer property hands out the raw connection with only a docstring asking callers to take write_txn, so the lock is enforced by convention; only tests reach it today.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/core/brain/store.py:304 The hatch is marked, and its invariant is written at store.py:243. But property 2 (enclosure) fails: the raw connection is reachable without passing the lock, which is the 'enclosed until the next call site' failure. tests/core/test_brain_reconcile.py already calls brain.writer.execute directly.
src/athena/core/brain/frontmatter.py:12 Divided by knowledge, not by order: frontmatter owns the byte format and store owns the order and meaning of keys.

src/athena/core/brain/reconcile.py:7 There is one insert path, so the rebuild cannot drift from incremental writes. WALK derives its scopes from paths.FACT_SCOPES and recall's floor reuses ALWAYS_IMPORTANCE.
src/athena/core/brain/frontmatter.py:84 The format parser and renderer are pure stdlib functions over strings; the header-injection refusal is testable with no doubles.
src/athena/core/brain/reconcile.py:109 One pass fills skipped, unsourced, files and by_kind and indexes as it goes (effects mixed in), so the explicit loop is the right form.
src/athena/core/brain/store.py:32 Threaded readers each get their own read-only handle rather than sharing the writer connection, so the carrier was chosen for the multi-threaded daemon.

src/athena/core/brain/store.py:322 The lock is the module's own logic (one writer, re-entrant, one transaction per memory). A sequential version would have to hand-write this coordination, so per the removal test it stays in the module.

pairs.subject: module-design
pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/src/modules/browser/model.ts:134 The browser module puts all its decisions in a pure selector over snapshots, with index.ts as the one file that knows a store exists, so model.test.ts and the preview fixtures exercise every branch with no shell.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/src/modules/browser/model.ts:134 selectBrowser is a pure function of snapshots; the hook in index.ts is the only driver.
apps/desktop/src/modules/browser/fixtures.ts:166 Fixtures are built through the real selector, with the actions seam wired to INERT, so a preview double cannot drift from the real model shape.
apps/desktop/src/modules/types.ts:4 The module contract hides store wiring behind one view-model; views take only the model and its actions.
apps/desktop/src/modules/browser/index.ts:43 Store lifecycle stays with the window roots; the module only reads.
apps/desktop/src/modules/browser/index.ts:72 Promise chains live only in the actions the hook wires; the selector and model are synchronous.
apps/desktop/src/modules/browser/model.ts:163 A single-output transformation from known origins to apps, written as a map/filter/map pipeline (the case where composition wins).

apps/desktop/src/modules/browser/model.ts:120 OriginsSnapshot is a plain snapshot of what the selector reads, but the store data is constructible as plain objects, so the technique's precondition (an input a test cannot construct) does not hold.
apps/desktop/src/modules/browser/model.ts:149 No wrapper forwards the IPC Tab: BrowserTab picks named fields explicitly instead of spreading, so implicit delegation does not occur.
